answer: The dry dock gates are caulked and measured each winter and the timber marks are filed with the dock master, and no ship may enter until the gates pass. A ocean gate patched with green timber fails the measure: at the plume of the dock the timbers must match the master's own file, and a patched gate leaks under pressure. Faking the gates means hiring shipwrights for a season, buying oak and paying 26,100, while the horizon mark on every timber is checked before each docking, so a gate whose timber was never filed is barred to shipping.
